I live here in Afar with my family, and the land is dry — rain comes little and late, so I must farm carefully with what Allah gives us. I have no money for chemical fertilizer, and the shops are far; I will put the manure from my goats and few cattle on the plot like my father did. For seed I keep my own sorghum from last harvest — it knows this soil and the dry wind. My wife and older children will help me weed and guard the crop from birds, and maybe I call one or two neighbors for a few days at harvest when the heads are heavy.
